newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- A group of Portuguese crime experts arrived in Macau to help tackle the enclave's crime wave, while an official from the public security bureau in China's southern Guangdong province was scheduled to hold meetings with his Macau counterpart.
-- SING TAO -- An provincial official in China's restive Xinjiang region confirmed the existence of organised separatist activities in the largely Moslem area.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- A member of the post-handover provisional legislature, Wong Siu-yee, has been receiving threatening phonecalls since he commented on the massacre at Tiananmen Square on June 4, 1989. In a speech at the beginning of the year, Wong said some people had to be sacrificed for the interests of the general public.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Last year, more than 9,000 Chinese state enterprises became shareholding companies. Economic experts said the moves would increase the competitiveness of state enterprises and help to establish a socialist market economy with Chinese characteristics.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Communist Party mouthpiece, the People's Daily, carried Chinese President Jiang Zemin's speech on strengthening patriotic education.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The vice-mayor of Dalian in northeastern China said the city was actively trying to attract Hong Kong investors to help develop a massive commercial centre designed by a U.S. firm. After Dalian's window company was listed in Hong Kong, it would also invest in the commercial centre, he said.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa was to send a roadshow from the Special Administrative Region, as Hong Kong will be called after China takes back the territory on July 1, on a tour of Europe, North America and Japan within months of the handover.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Wharf Cable escaped a hefty pay-out in a U.S. court case it lost last week to a former business partner, U.S. cable television company United International Holdings.
-- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority tightened its guidelines on "cash-collateralised loans" in an effort to improve the credit quality of local banks.
